stops.date_confidence: attested. World premiere 8 March 1945 at the Teatro Avenida, Avenida de Mayo 1222, Buenos Aires, by the company of Margarita Xirgu (en.wikipedia, 'The House of Bernarda Alba'; es.wikipedia, 'Teatro Avenida'). The working material carried this stop with a positive latitude, plotting it in Iraq; corrected here to -34.6094, -58.3839.

stops.segment: The Grave That Was Never Found
stops.stop: Granada, the two-page report
stops.date_confidence: [R] pending direct verification. The 9 July 1965 Granada police report, produced after Marcelle Auclair's inquiries, is cited by the dossier to RTVE's summary of 23 April 2015; rtve.es blocked direct fetch in this pass and the document itself was not read. No lodge register corroborating the Masonry charge has been located. Pinned to the Gobierno Civil, the building where the arrest was recorded. The quoted line is a verified Kline translation; note that the widely circulated variant 'more alive than a dead man anywhere in the world' is attested nowhere but Wikiquote.

stops.segment: The Grave That Was Never Found
stops.stop: Buenos Aires, Jardín de los Poetas: the bronze head
stops.date_confidence: attested. Bronze bust on a concrete base by Eduardo Carretero (1920-2011), municipal art inventory MOA no. 2477, inaugurated 19 August 1986, the fiftieth anniversary of the killing, plaque crediting the Provincial Delegation of Granada and the Argentine Republic, per the weboeba.com municipal-art inventory record. Circulating claims of a 2014 date or a design by Takutaro Yabushi belong to other objects in the Rosedal. Coordinates are the corpus's canonical Jardín de los Poetas pin, inherited byte-for-byte from carlos_thays.journey.json through jose_marti.journey.json; the corpus holds two other pins for the same garden, -34.575/-58.414 in taras_shevchenko.journey.json and -34.5706/-58.4173 in troiano_troiani.journey.json, and weboeba gives -34.5721/-58.4136 for this bust. The discrepancy is recorded, not resolved.

stops.segment: The Grave That Was Never Found
stops.stop: Fuente Grande and the Barranco de Víznar, the digging
stops.date_confidence: attested. University of Granada excavation October-December 2009 in the Parque Federico García Lorca by Fuente Grande, costing about 70,000 euros, finding bedrock at 40 cm and no confirmed remains; a 2014 dig under Miguel Caballero Pérez less than half a kilometre away, also inconclusive; a 2016 well theory unsubstantiated (en.wikipedia). For the ravine at Víznar, es.wikipedia states 166 bodies recovered and seven civilian victims identified as of 2025, correcting the figure of roughly 132 that was in circulation. Coordinates are the Fuente Grande ground; the ravine excavations lie nearby to the west of Alfacar.
